diagnostics.message: module.webhook-github-app:resource.null_resource.update_app registers the webhook URL in the GitHub App via a local-exec provisioner using module.runners.webhook.endpoint, which resolves to "${aws_apigatewayv2_api.webhook.api_endpoint}/webhook". That path only traces back to the API object (and the lambda), not to module.runners.module.webhook:resource.aws_apigatewayv2_stage.webhook (the "$default" stage), so on a fresh apply the GitHub App can be pointed at a URL that is not yet served, and GitHub's verification ping will 404. The registration step should be ordered after the API stage is deployed (e.g. by exporting an endpoint that references the stage and depending on it). No idiomatic data-reference fix exists here because null_resource has no attribute that can reference the other module's stage.

module.runners:resource.aws_sqs_queue_policy.build_queue_dlq_policy is the dead-letter-queue policy (count = var.redrive_build_queue.enabled), but its queue_url points at aws_sqs_queue.queued_builds instead of the dead-letter queue, so it never establishes any ordering against module.runners:resource.aws_sqs_queue.queued_builds_dlq. In practice it both races with the DLQ's creation and silently overwrites the primary build queue policy (a queue has a single policy), so the DLQ ends up without the deny-unsecure-transport policy. Setting queue_url to the DLQ ARN/id restores both the intended behaviour and an implicit dependency.
